papers_read.title_as_printed: The Coupled Representation of Hierarchical Features for Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease Classification (Liu, Li, Yao, Guo; Front. Neurosci. 2022, 16:902528)
Biomarker Extraction Based on Subspace Learning for the Prediction of Mild Cognitive Impairment Conversion (Li, Fang, Wang, Zhang, Hu; BioMed Research International 2021, 5531940)

what_each_reports.P-207: ADNI baseline structural MRI (VBM grey-matter volume, ICA-derived networks, two-level coupled features, AdaBoost with linear-SVM base learners, 10-fold CV). AD vs NC (121/120): best accuracy 90.44% (sens 88.5, spec 93.67). MCI-c vs MCI-nc (126/108, conversion within 3 years): best accuracy 87.72% (sens 84.16, spec 91.64). The 90.44% is the AD vs NC figure, not a conversion result. No AUC reported.
what_each_reports.P-185: ADNI baseline 1.5T structural MRI (FreeSurfer regional cortical thickness and volume, subspace projection learned on 142 AD / 165 NC, applied to 126 pMCI / 95 sMCI with a 3-year conversion window), 10-fold CV repeated 20 times. Best pMCI vs sMCI accuracy 69.37% (linear SVM; sens 75.39, spec 61.23, AUC 0.6951).

quantity_a: As recorded: accuracy for AD vs NC (90.44%). The paper's own conversion figure is accuracy for MCI-c vs MCI-nc (3-year window), ADNI baseline sMRI, ICA-network coupled GMV features, 10-fold CV: 87.72%.
quantity_b: Accuracy for pMCI vs sMCI (3-year window), ADNI baseline sMRI, FreeSurfer cortical thickness/volume subspace biomarkers, 20 x 10-fold CV: 69.37%.
incompatible_if_same: No. Even taking P-207's genuine conversion figure (87.72%) against P-185's 69.37% on the same nominal task, these are two different feature pipelines each reporting its own cross-validated accuracy; neither study evaluates the other's method or claims an ordering that the other refutes, so both results can be true.

gates.task: mismatch as recorded (P-207's 90.44% is AD vs NC, not T2); match if P-207's MCI-c vs MCI-nc 87.72% is substituted (both 3-year pMCI vs sMCI)
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI baseline MRI (different, possibly overlapping subject subsets)
gates.modality_family: match: both structural MRI (the registry's 'EEG/MEG' for P-207 is wrong; the paper uses T1 MPRAGE sMRI only)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded: the claim sets an AD vs NC accuracy against a pMCI vs sMCI accuracy. Same metric type (accuracy) and same 3-year conversion endpoint only once P-207's 87.72% is used, but input representations differ (ICA-network coupled GMV features vs FreeSurfer thickness/volume subspace features).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither study reaches 0.97 (P-207 max 90.44%, P-185 69.37%); this is a between-method performance comparison, not one resting on a near-ceiling study.
independence: Distinct author groups (Beijing Normal University vs Shandong/Lanzhou); both draw on ADNI and may share subjects; no shared authorship.
grounds: The record's P-207 figure (90.44%) is its AD vs NC accuracy, so the claim misreads the paper as a conversion (T2) result.

P-207's actual conversion accuracy (87.72%) and P-185's 69.37% are scores of two different feature pipelines, and neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes, so the two results are compatible.

The two studies also differ in input representation (ICA-network coupled GMV vs FreeSurfer cortical thickness/volume), which is why their accuracies are not a measurement disagreement about one quantity.

evidence_quotes.quote: the best prediction accuracy is 90.44%, sensitivity is 88.5%, and specificity is 93.67% for AD and NC groups and the best prediction accuracy is 87.72%, sensitivity is 84.16%, and specificity is 91.64% for the MCI-c and MCI-nc groups.
The patients with MCI who converted to AD within 3-year follow-up were classified into the MCI-c group; otherwise, they were classified into the MCI-nc group.
The 10-fold cross-validation was applied to evaluate the performance, and the average results were reported.
The proposed biomarker achieved highest accuracy of 69.37% when using SVM classifier with linear kernel.
We use baseline MRI scans (1.5 T ...) of 528 subjects, which include 142 AD subjects, 165 NC subjects, and 221 MCI subjects. Moreover, the 221 MCI subjects contain 126 pMCI and 95 sMCI subjects.
we repeated 10-fold cross-validation 20 times to report the average results for each method.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-207: Acc 90.44 on T2' is wrong: 90.44% is P-207's AD vs NC accuracy; its MCI-c vs MCI-nc (T2) accuracy is 87.72%.
The pack's registry row gives P-207 Modality 'EEG/MEG' and Task_Type 'T4'; the paper is structural MRI only and reports AD vs NC plus MCI-c vs MCI-nc classification.
gap_magnitude 0.211 is computed from the misread AD vs NC figure; the like-for-like conversion gap is 0.184 (87.72 vs 69.37).
resolution_note's rejection ground 'Modality mismatch: P-207=EEG vs P-185=structural_MRI' is false; both are structural MRI (the verdict stands on other grounds).
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only a paper in which one group evaluated the other's method (or both methods on a common split) and reported an ordering opposite to the other's; neither PDF contains such a comparison.
